en.name: Anthony Zaccaria
en.summary: Italian physician turned priest who founded the Barnabites and pioneered public devotional practices later common across the Church.
en.body: Anthony Zaccaria trained and practiced as a physician in his native Cremona before feeling called to the priesthood, bringing a doctor's practical attentiveness to human suffering into his subsequent pastoral work. In Milan he founded the Clerics Regular of St. Paul, known as the Barnabites after the church of St. Barnabas where they were based, a community of priests dedicated to preaching reform and renewed fervor among laypeople at a time, just before the Council of Trent, when the wider Church badly needed it. He was an early and energetic promoter of practices that would later become common Catholic devotions, including frequent reception of communion by laypeople, public exposition of the Blessed Sacrament, and the ringing of church bells on Friday afternoons in memory of Christ's Passion, all somewhat novel or contested in his own time. He died in 1539 at only thirty-six, worn out by his intense ministry, and was canonized in 1897.
